question: Who is Colocation Technology Services?
detail: The 2026-10-12 sweep found no web footprint for the developer the City names. On 2026-10-18 one turned up: colotech.co, whose footer reads "© 2026 Colocation Technology Services LLC". It is the company's self-description: a "300+ MWs Development Pipeline" and six delivered campuses, but no Ohio project, no address and no officer. That it is the company that approached WAEDC rests on the name alone ([inference]). The instrument that closes this is still the SOS record (formation date, statutory agent, foreign or domestic), which needs a browser. Never resolve "CTS" by acronym: QTS, the Van Wert operator, is a different company.
source: City of Wapakoneta Facebook statement (undated); Wapakoneta Daily News 2026-10-08; colotech.co capture 2026-10-18 · data/extracted/wapakoneta/data-centers.md

question: The City's post describes 50 MW; the press reports a path to 70 acres and 200 MW
detail: The City's statement describes "a smaller sized data center" requiring 50 MW. The Wapakoneta Daily News (2026-10-08), reporting WAEDC's briefing to Council, adds "the potential to eventually expand to 70 acres and 200 megawatts." The AEP feasibility result the City relays ("could be served without improvements") is stated for the 50 MW load. Whether it covers the ceiling is unknown. JobsOhio lists the West Central Ohio Industrial Center at 5 MW of excess electric capacity. The feasibility study itself, via a records request to the City, is the instrument.
source: Wapakoneta Daily News 2026-10-08; City Facebook statement; JobsOhio WCOIC listing · data/extracted/wapakoneta/data-centers.md §1.2–1.3

question: Where does the hauled cooling water go?
detail: CTS says its closed-loop cooling water "would not be discharged into the City's sewer system but would instead be periodically removed and properly disposed of off-site." A hauled waste stream lands at someone's permit, whether a POTW that receives trucked waste or an industrial treater. That receiver, and the blowdown chemistry it is permitted to take, is the water question this design moves rather than answers.
source: City of Wapakoneta Facebook statement (undated) · data/extracted/wapakoneta/data-centers.md §1.4

question: What does Ord. 2024-48 actually condition?
detail: The City says Council made data centers "a conditional use" in 2024. The instruments are Ord. 2024-48, amending §1282.04 (M-3 Industrial District conditional uses), and Ord. 2024-46, amending the §1250.10(174) "warehouse" definition. Both were adopted 7-0 on 2024-11-18, and neither title says "data center." The codified text is now read (American Legal, supplement S-27): a functional "Data Warehouse (Center)" definition with no size threshold, admitted only as an M-3 conditional use. The review is the generic §1252.07 one: eight findings, none specific to data centers, and a hearing only if the Planning Commission wants one. The ordinances as signed are still not in hand, so whether the codifier carried them faithfully is unchecked. The 2024 minutes (now held) record that at the second reading the Planning Commission had made no comment, no utility-rate conversation had occurred and the City's engineering consultant had given no input; both ordinances were adopted at the next meeting with no recorded discussion.

question: The City's statement exists in no archive
detail: The City Administration's Facebook statement is the only source for the City's no-negotiation, no-commitment position and for the AEP feasibility result. Facebook serves no dated page to a script, and the Wayback Machine has no snapshot. Today the register holds only a pasted transcription. Capture the post with its date before it can be edited or removed.
